summary.text: A 63-year-old woman contacted a toxicology department reporting numerous neurological disorders that had persisted, in a context of diagnostic wandering, and was referred to internal medicine. Her history included a major depressive syndrome with asthenia and sick leave in 2017, abnormally high urinary lead and mercury in May 2018 followed by six monthly intravenous chelation treatments, and follow-up BLLs of 72 μg/L in October 2018 and 83 μg/L in January 2021.

At the internal medicine consultation in August 2021 she reported increasingly marked neurological disorders with memory disturbances, spatial disorientation, immediate memory issues, headaches and nearly constant tingling in the fingers and face. MRI and the clinical examination were normal, blood count and electrolytes showed no abnormalities, eGFR was >90 mL/min, hemoglobin was 13.7 g/dL, and BLL was elevated at 170 μg/L, with an increase noted in August 2021; no peripheral blood film was performed.

A report was made to the poison control centre and the Regional Health Agency requested an investigation of environmental contamination; her two children (men aged 24 and 27) had BLLs within the normal population range. Occupational exposure as a dental surgeon was considered but not suggested. A BLL of 198 μg/L followed in January 2022, and in April 2022 a phone conversation raised the suspicion that kohl, applied to her eye contours every morning and afternoon since age 20, was the source.

She immediately ceased using kohl; the four kohl samples, bought in Morocco in 1980, 1984, 2017 and 2021 and alternately reused, contained 67.7-79.3 % lead with mercury and cadmium below the limit of detection, confirming kohl as the identified source. About two months after stopping her BLL was 98 μg/L, and lead concentrations took a year to fall below 50 μg/L. She had replaced kohl with an organic cosmetic between 2019 and early 2021 before resuming it.

Her BLL is monitored every 3-6 months, and absorption and elimination constants were estimated from the curve. In March 2023 blood count, electrolytes, eGFR and hemoglobin were unremarkable, and in July 2023 plasma and whole blood metal values showed no abnormal values after a urinary metal screen. Chelation with dimercaptosuccinic acid was not proposed. In February 2024 she felt better but had sudden episodes of intense fatigue.
